# 2013 ULTIMATE ASCENT – hindsight

Source: user hindsight notes, batch 1 (2026-09-27).

## Game play / meta
- **Full-court shooters vs low-rider cyclists.** Human-player loading was the meta: it was faster to load 4 discs
  quickly this way (without them being stolen). Ground clean-up was useful, especially in AUTO, but it was not the meta.
- Elite alliances had full-court shooters and used them until they got defended, then switched to cycles: three-robot
  cycles, or two cyclers plus one ground clean-up.
- Most teams climbed only to the first level; **1114 and 118 had very effective climbers to the third level**.

## Dominant robots
- **2056 / 469** – ground intake below the robot.
- **1986** – a dustpan mechanism used only in AUTO, to collect discs from the floor and drop them from above into their
  feeding mechanism (the same one the human player loads during the match). Super simple and effective.

## Effective mechanisms
- **118 active human-player intake** – rollers to speed up loading from the human player.
- **2630 shooter** – large pneumatic wheel with a curved back wall; 2630 managed full-court shots.
- **2056 / 1114 / 1986** – double sets of small wheels with a straight back wall.
- **118 deflection** – a horizontal plate that deflects the disc's exit angle instead of rotating the whole mechanism.
- **2630 passive climber** – opens with a latch; then you just drive onto the level-1 rung and get wedged on it.
- **1114 level-3 climber** – very fast: one extending hook and one static hook, under the robot.
- **1577 blocking net** – flex rods with a net; a rope winch lowers it so the robot could pass under the pyramid.
- To make the pyramid shot "safe", teams effectively just used a floppy zip tie that still touched the pyramid –
  simple and effective.
